tool: Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.5.15 in print mode, run in an empty directory outside the repository: `agy -p "<request>" --model gemini-4-neon-high --mode accept-edits --sandbox --output-format json`. The agent hands the request to its built-in image-generator subagent, which writes the image prompt and calls its generate_image tool.
model: gemini-3.1-flash-image behind generate_image (the service named it in a capacity error of the same session; the tool does not report it on success); agent gemini-4-neon-high; image-generator subagent gemini-4-hydrogen-tiered-high.
prompt: Full-frame square photograph of a clean medium grey epoxy-coated concrete industrial factory floor texture, single continuous non-repeating surface across the entire image (no repeated 2x2 grid patterns). Viewed strictly straight-on orthographic top-down 90 degrees, zero perspective. Completely flat uniform even diffuse lighting, no shadows, no specular highlights, no glare, no vignetting. Medium neutral grey epoxy resin over concrete with subtle organic soft mottling, evenly distributed tiny fine aggregate speckles, very fine micro-scratches and faint delicate scuff marks spread naturally and uniformly from edge to edge. No joints, no seams, no lines, no cracks, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings. Uniform brightness and detail across all edges for clean 3D material tiling, photorealistic.
request: Generate exactly one image with aspect ratio 1:1 and nothing else. Image description: A seamless tileable surface texture of a clean industrial factory floor in medium grey epoxy-coated concrete: subtle soft mottling, fine aggregate speckles and faint fine scuff marks, no joints, no painted lines, viewed perfectly straight on (orthographic, top-down), completely flat even diffuse lighting, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no perspective, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings, uniform detail across the whole frame so it can tile seamlessly in a 3D material, photorealistic, square.
postProcessing: 1. ImageMagick 7.1.2-36, a one-off conversion of the generated JPEG to an 8-bit RGB PNG: `magick source.jpg -strip -colorspace sRGB -type TrueColor PNG24:source.png`. 2. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts prepare floor source.png`: the last 128 columns and rows are cross-faded into the first ones (seamless, 896x896), the broad light and shade is removed (a wrapping box blur of radius 112 subtracted, the mean kept), and the image is area-averaged to 512x512. 3. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` writes normal.png, roughness.png and metalness.png from basecolor.png. 4. 2026-11-24, after the owner's review of the pilot: until then the renderer tiled the floor a hundred times too finely, so its relief had never shown; at its real scale (one tile per 2 m) it read as a rough, wavy surface, not an epoxy coat. The recipe of this material in tools/plant/textures.ts became heightBlur 3, normalStrength 0.06 (it was heightBlur 2, normalStrength 0.4), and `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` wrote normal.png again; basecolor.png, roughness.png and metalness.png did not change.
